---
title: "{cli} evaluates everything between braces"
ref: STR-06
categories: [Strings]
impact: cryptique
attendu: "the message `Please install {packacode}` as is"
versions: "All versions of {cli}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2022)"
---

::: {.piege packages="cli"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(cli))

cli_alert_danger("Please install {packacode}")
cli_text("Expected format: {\"a\": 1}")
```
:::

## Why

{cli} functions interpret their text the way {glue} does: whatever sits between braces is R code, evaluated when the message is displayed. `{packacode}` looks for a variable `packacode`, which does not exist. A JSON example between braces becomes the expression `"a": 1`, a sequence from `"a"` to `1`, which fails with "NA/NaN argument".

The pitfall mostly strikes error messages: the code meant to report a problem fails itself, with an unrelated message.

## The remedy

Double the braces to display them, or pass the text through a variable.

::: {.piege packages="cli"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(cli))

cli_alert_danger("Please install {{packacode}}")

pkg <- "packacode"
cli_alert_danger("Please install {.pkg {pkg}}")
```
:::
